Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the usage file.

We can absolutely support a mid-contract amendment that blends the uplift into your existing term (avoids a separate top-up contract). I'm sending a preliminary "FlexPlay" amendment idea that tries to balance unit economics and runway flexibility:

Summary of proposed approach (FlexPlay v1):
- Convert uplift into a staged committed increase: +40% effective immediately, with a 6-month grace true-up window (we true-up to actuals at month 6).
- Blended pricing: offer a 12% blended discount on the uplifted units (applies to the incremental 40% for the remainder of the current term).
- Co-term: we will align the uplift to the existing agreement end date; next renewal will reflect the new baseline.
- Seats/priority: include a burst buffer of +10% for peak traffic, billed at a slightly higher unit rate unless used.

Deliverables: I can send an amendment draft and a one-page SOW summary for legal. If that looks good, we'll send to your procurement and include a DocuSign-ready amendment.

I've attached the FlexPlay one-pager and a draft proposal for numbers. Can you confirm who from procurement should receive the DocuSign? Also, what is your internal SLA/exec approval target date for this?

Proposed meeting: Tue 5/4 at 11am PT to review numbers (30m).

Best,

Folks — forwarding SprintScale thread. Key asks: mid-contract +40% blended into term, looking to keep blended unit-rate increase <= ~15%. Procurement will want a DocuSign-ready amendment and a minimal SOW.

My read: we can give them an efficient FlexPlay (staged commit + true-up) but to hold margin I'd like to explore conditional discounting tied to:
- minimum uplift commit (e.g., commit to sustaining at least 25% of uplift for remainder),
- prepayment or quarterly invoicing, or
- 12-month extension at renewal (optional).

Can you propose a concrete pricing and discount matrix? Also confirm whether a 12% blended discount on the incremental units is acceptable from finance. If not, what floor do we have for a one-off midterm amendment?

Goal: produce a short amendment (1-2 pages) + SOW + DocuSign link by EOD Thu 5/6.

Thanks — Priya

Agree with your approach. Finance guidance: floor for a midterm blended uplift discount is 10% on incremental units unless there's a longer-term extension or prepay. Given SprintScale size and the +40% uplift, we should target 12% as an OK middle ground, but tie it to either:

- a 9-month minimum retention threshold on at least 60% of the uplifted volume, OR
- a 6-month prepayment for the uplifted portion (discount increases to 15% if they prepay Q3+Q4).

Also recommend we add a simple performance clause: if 6-month average usage after uplift is below 60% of the uplift, we reserve right to re-price for the remainder of the term. That protects unit economics.

I'll draft a quick pricing matrix and a short legal-safe clause; Ben, can you confirm DocuSign workflow and whether Legal needs any special vendor code?

— Priyom
